title: PNG Chiefs forms 10-brand partnership portfolio ahead of 2028 debut
article_text:
The PNG Chiefs, the newest expansion franchise in Australia’s top-tier National Rugby League (NRL), has sold out its commercial playing kit inventory ahead of its 2028 launch.

Ten founding partners have been established ahead of the Papua New Guinea-based franchise’s debut 2028 campaign, ranging from prominent international brands, regional heavyweights, and local partners.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Bank South Pacific, the regional banking heavyweight, will be the principal partner of the PNG Chiefs, taking up the primary front-of-shirt sponsorship slot through the 2030 campaign (supporting the club’s first three seasons).

This is supported by three secondary ‘premier partners’, liquefied natural gas producer PNG LNG (upper back of jersey sponsor), local financial services brand Numbawan Super (lower back of shirt sponsor), and soft drinks giant Coca-Cola (sleeve sponsor).

The jersey inventory is rounded out by two third-tier ‘major partners’, agriculture and food supply firm Taylor Pacific, which is planting its logo on the sternum of the jersey, and regional Toyota dealer ELA Motors, which places the Toyota brand on the jersey shoulders.

A trio of locally-based major partners have also taken up sponsorship on the team’s shorts. Regional airline Air Niugini will be the front-of-short sponsor, while the K92 Mining business (headquartered in Canada but operating in Papua New Guinea) and South Pacific Brewery (SP Brewery) are the back-of-shorts sponsors.

Finally, Australian sportswear manufacturer Struddys, the club’s official apparel and kit partner and another in the major partner tier, will take branding presence on PNG Chiefs merchandise, including replica kits, which it will also sell.

Speaking on the announcement of these 10 partners, PNG Chiefs chief executive Lorna McPherson commented: “Seeing our first-ever playing kit filled with partners who are proudly Papua New Guinean and proudly standing alongside us fills me with great pride.

“It’s a proud moment for both the PNG Chiefs and our country, and having their support shows there is a genuine belief in what we’re building and the important role that this club can play for the people of Papua New Guinea.

“We’re incredibly thankful to our foundation partners for their support, both now and as we mark our official entry into the competition in 2028, and we look forward to them joining us on the journey as we proudly represent the people of Papua New Guinea.”

Per the GlobalData Sport NRL 2026 Sponsor Grid, the average NRL franchise receives around US$9.8 million per year in sponsorship revenue. As a new franchise, playing in a less economically developed region, the Chiefs will likely fall under that; however, the early move to secure a raft of major partners already shows that the team has a strong commercial baseline.

The establishment of the Chiefs franchise, which is financially backed by the government of Australia, is effectively a soft power play by the Australian government to bring Papua New Guinea closer to Australia diplomatically, in opposition to growing influence in the region from economic rival China.

Australia’s government will dispense as much as A$600 million (US$410 million) in funding to support the Chiefs over the first decade of its existence, with the aim of making the franchise financially self-sustainable by 2037.

Federal government funding will be dispensed in stages, with the first A$60 million assigned to fund the team’s license fee (A$3.5 million each for the league’s 17 current sides), A$290 million to fund the team over its first 10 years of operations, while the remaining A$250 million will be utilized for community initiatives, education, and infrastructure development.

Papua New Guinea’s export economy is centered around its natural commodity wealth, including valuable minerals like gold, copper, and cobalt, oil, liquefied natural gas, and agricultural products, making it a sought-after regional trade partner, with Australia, China, and Japan all competing for leverage in the market.

Australia, obviously, benefits from its close geographical and perhaps cultural ties to Papua New Guinea, and the establishment of the Chiefs, which comes with A$250 million in Australian government funding specifically marked for community initiatives, education, and infrastructure development, is a key part of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese’s play for stronger relations across the Pacific.

That businesses from the prominent aforementioned export sectors, including PNG LNG, K92 Mining, and Taylor Pacific, are represented in the first round of PNG Chiefs sponsors perhaps serves as an early proof of concept for Australia’s investment in the team.

title: DirecTV to carry regional channels of four NHL teams
article_text:
US cable TV heavyweight DirecTV has announced a new multi-year distribution agreement with the National Hockey League (NHL) to carry the new regional channels of the Carolina Hurricanes, Columbus Blue Jackets, Minnesota Wild, and St. Louis Blues

Through the agreement, Hurricanes Hockey Network, Blue Jackets Hockey Network, Wild+, and Blue Note+ will be available to DirecTV streaming and satellite customers who live in each team’s NHL-designated home territory.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Subscribers will have access to pregame, postgame, and in-game live sports services.

The agreement also provides distribution rights to each NHL team to all of DirecTV For Business’s sports bars, restaurants, fitness clubs, and other commercial venues located within each team’s respective region.

DirecTV recently obtained regional or local rights to 76 of the 81 US-based NHL, NBA (basketball), or MLB (baseball) franchises, including multi-year agreements for 23 US-based hockey teams.

Rob Thun, chief content officer at DirecTV, said: “We are committed to keeping fans connected to their favorite teams and giving them more choice and flexibility in how they watch and what they pay.

“As local sports distribution evolves, DirecTV brings team channels, regional sports networks, and other viewing options together to make it easier for fans to follow their teams.”

title: RTL retains Oktagon rights through 2031
article_text:
European mixed martial arts (MMA) promotion Oktagon has renewed its broadcast deal with commercial broadcaster RTL Deutschland until 2031.

Through the four-year renewal, every Oktagon event will continue to stream on the RTL+ platform in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Luxembourg, and Liechtenstein.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

In addition, selected events and fights will air nationwide on free-to-air channel RTL. Both sides are also collaborating to develop new TV and digital formats.

The promotion has staged several major events in Germany in recent years, most notably last month when Oktagon 94 at Frankfurt’s Deutsche Bank Park soccer stadium drew an attendance of 57,000 fans.

The upcoming Oktagon 96 event will be held in Germany on Saturday (October 31) at Munich’s SAP Garden.

Ondřej Novotný, Oktagon co-founder, said: “We’re thrilled that after less than two years on this journey together, our partnership with RTL has proven so successful that the group decided to significantly extend the contract.

“It gives our great partners, led by RTL, as well as our fighters and fans the certainty that Oktagon will remain Europe’s clear number one in MMA, in every respect.”

Inga Leschek, chief content officer of RTL Deutschland, added: “With Oktagon, we are seeing live how fast MMA is moving forward in Germany. Almost 60,000 fans in Frankfurt, record ratings on free-to-air TV and more than a million views on RTL+ are clear proof of that.

“The quality of the fight cards keeps rising, new stars are emerging, and the fan base keeps growing. That is exactly why we are extending our partnership until 2031. Together, we will reach the next generation of fans and firmly establish MMA in the sporting mainstream.”

title: Valencia sell 42% to consortium, Viessmann buys minority stake in Bayern
article_text:
The continued growth in sports property valuations through the 2020s has led to a raft of new investors entering the European soccer space.

In recent days, it was revealed that a consortium including the founders of private equity giant KKR and the prominent Walton-Penner family has acquired a large minority stake in historic Spanish soccer side Valencia CF.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

This deal, for 42% of the club, values Valencia at €1.25 billion ($1.4 billion), pricing the transaction at €525 million, with the new investors also putting a further €100 million of investment into the side immediately.

The group, termed Pitchwise Holdings, is led by investor pair Ann Rodriguez and Corey Woolfolk, and includes backing from KKR co-founders George Roberts and Henry Kravis, as well as Penner Sports Group, the investment vehicle of Greg and Carrie Walton-Penner.

Penner Sports Group is part owner of the NFL’s Denver Broncos franchise, and earlier this year acquired a 40% stake in the Colorado Rockies Major League Baseball team.

Kiat Lim, Valencia’s president, will remain in place, alongside Rodriguez and Woolfolk in the new ownership group, with his side of the ownership mix, Meriton Holdings, remaining majority shareholder of 57% of the LaLiga club.

On the investment, Lim said: “There has been no shortage of interest in Valencia; the Pitchwise team was the only partnership I was keen to pursue. They bring long-term investment expertise and sports acumen.

“I am confident that we are entering a new era and we can achieve great things for Valencia CF. Together we will build a modern club whose men's and women's teams compete consistently in Europe, whose academy produces world-class talent, and whose new home at Nou Mestalla becomes a landmark for the city and the entire region of Valencia."

In the 2024-25 season, the club generated €103.7 million in revenue, making an operating profit of €23.8 million over the period.

A valuation of €1.25 billion is lofty for a Valencia team that, on the pitch, has struggled to offer much in the way of promise for supporters over the past few years.

Valencia have not finished above ninth in LaLiga since the 2018-29 campaign, and have flirted with relegation multiple times in that period.

Currently, after 10 games, Valencia sit second-to-last in LaLiga, having won only once in the league so far this year.

Despite that, the club’s operations off the pitch are what have really powered this valuation, chief among them the 70,000-capacity Nou Mestalla stadium project, which will be completed this year, giving the team a new home after over 100 years.

Valencia are expecting to generate as much as three times the stadium revenue from their new home, compared to what they are currently drawing at their ‘used-up’ Mestalla home.

Upon completion, the Nou Mestalla will boast the fourth-highest capacity of any stadium in LaLiga, and will be one of the 15 largest stadia in Europe, surpassing Munich’s Allianz Arena, Seville’s Estadio de la Cartuja, and London’s Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Crucially, with that expanded capacity (around 20,000 seats more than the current Mestalla) comes access to new revenue streams that the current venue’s restrictions simply rule out.

Matchday revenue reportedly accounts for about a quarter of Valencia CF’s annual turnover, so if Segarra is correct and the stadium increases that figure by as much as three times, then overall club revenues could increase by 50% within a year of opening.

Elsewhere in European soccer, record German champions FC Bayern Munich have also sold a minority stake, just under 6.7% in all, to Viessmann Generations Group, bringing in a rare external investor.

The club, majority fan-owned as most clubs in Germany are, has been valued at €3.73 billion through the transaction, which is reportedly worth €250 million.

The majority shareholding of the fan-ownership association (termed FC Bayern München eV) now stands at 70%, while the other three external investors in the club- sportswear giant Adidas, car brand Audi, and insurance firm Allianz – have had their stakes diluted from 8.33% to just under 7.8%, meaning minority investors hold 30% of the club in all.

Viessmann, the heating tech firm, has been a sponsor of FC Bayern since 2018, and the company’s head Max Viessmann, who leads the Viessmann Generations Group family office, is a noted fan of FC Bayern.

On the deal, Viessmann himself said: “FC Bayern and Viessmann have worked closely together since 2018. We are now taking the next step by becoming a shareholder of FC Bayern.

“As a fourth-generation family business, we want to contribute both capital and our entrepreneurial experience to the collaboration. We want to play our part in maintaining a strong FC Bayern – a club with its own identity, economic independence and sustained success.”

Read more – Is the Nou Mestalla the key to Valencia CF's financial revival?

title: Fin Smith injury scare leads to change to England training squad
article_text:
Gloucester fly-half Charlie Atkinson has been rewarded for his club form with a place in England’s training squad for the upcoming Nations Championship.

The 25-year-old has been brought in as cover for Fin Smith, who suffered a calf injury in Northampton’s derby day defeat to Leicester on Saturday.

Atkinson, who won his only England cap against USA in the summer of 2025, has been pivotal to Gloucester’s strong start to the season.

The Cherry & Whites lead the PREM table after the opening four rounds, while in the Champions Cup, they held holders Bordeaux-Begles to a draw.

Smith was named as part of a 36-man training squad by head coach Steve Borthwick on Sunday, but will not train this week and instead begin his rehabilitation in camp.

The Saints star has taken a grip on the 10 jersey since the last two rounds of the Six Nations, starting all three of the July Tests against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina.

A calf injury forced him to miss the start of the Championship with George Ford selected as chief conductor and the veteran Sale playmaker will come into contention to deputise if Smith is ruled out.

Marcus Smith is the third fly-half in England’s elite player squad and the Harlequin entered camp on Sunday night as a player in form following his man of the match performance against Saracens hours earlier.

Smith celebrated his 200th appearance for Quins by running in the first try and stopping Max Malins from touching down with a last-gasp tackle in an emphatic 33-15 victory at The Stoop.

However, Borthwick sees Smith primarily as a full-back rather than fly-half where he plays for Quins, with the 27-year-old also a vital bench option because of his ability to cover multiple positions.

England have begun a three-day training camp ahead of the forthcoming Nations Championship. The squad will train at England’s Performance Centre at Pennyhill Park until Tuesday 27 October.

England welcome Australia to Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on Sunday 8 November in Round 4 of the Nations Championship, before taking on Japan and New Zealand.

title: SPFL plugs in Smart Energy GB to sponsorship roster with TV graphics deal
article_text:
October 26 – The SPFL has added Smart Energy GB to its commercial roster in a league-wide deal that will put the organisation alongside live score and clock graphics during Scottish Premiership broadcasts.

Smart Energy GB becomes both the league’s Official Smart Meter Partner and Official Timing Partner, with its branding also appearing on every SPFL club’s digital substitution board.

It is the first time an SPFL-wide commercial partner has been given that particular piece of inventory, while Premier Sports coverage will also carry specially produced advertising bumpers featuring players.

The agreement has been delivered through Scottish Football Marketing – the centralised commercial operation working across the SPFL, Scottish Women’s Premier League and Scottish FA.

A new ‘Smart Energy GB Save of the Month’ award will also form part of the activation, adding a slightly more football-specific hook to a partnership built around promoting smart meters and household energy awareness.

Smart Energy GB is a non-profit organisation tasked with helping households and small businesses understand smart meter technology. It has used sport before, including through partnerships with the EFL and Professional Darts Corporation.

The deal lands at a useful time for the SPFL, whose latest accounts showed record group distributions of £49.6 million to clubs, up £7.6 million year-on-year, with total group income reaching £58 million. Fees paid directly to clubs also increased 17% to £41.2 million.

Neil Doncaster, SPFL group chief executive, said: “Smart Energy GB has shown commitment to helping sports fans manage their energy bills and we’re proud that they are now taking that message to a Scottish audience through the SPFL.

“Having recently announced record payments to clubs across the SPFL, we know the value that such partnerships have in growing our game and we look forward to building a strong working relationship with the team at Smart Energy GB.”

title: New Welsh Rugby Union chairman gives hope to regions facing axe
article_text:
Lyndon Faulkner has a frank message for anyone who believes that one of the stipulations in his appointment as chairman of the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) was to back the toxic plan of cutting the number of regions.

“I am not a yes man and I wouldn’t be taking the job if they were needing me to be that,” Faulkner said. “Look at my resume – I’m just not a yes man. And there has been some talk out there that whoever took this job was under the condition that they can’t talk about the four to three regions or the four to two or whatever it’s going to be. But that is absolutely incorrect.

“I wouldn’t have taken the job with those conditions. So I feel it’s my role to look at everything we’ve got going on, challenge it, probe it, and hopefully bring my experience to bear.”

Faulkner’s comments in his first interview since being named two weeks ago as the replacement for Richard Collier-Keywood will give hope to the masses opposed to the WRU proposals.

Since these were unveiled almost exactly a year ago, a sporting civil war has brewed, with the tensions at least partly to blame for the likes of big names such as Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake departing the domestic scene to play their club rugby in England.

The WRU has squarely, and quite unashamedly, targeted one of the Ospreys or the Scarlets, declaring that finances dictate there will be one team in Gwent – the Dragons – the Cardiff team in the capital and one in the west. The Scarlets or the Ospreys, Llanelli or Swansea? Pick your hotbed to disappear to the scrapheap – or merge.

title: Joe Marchant recalled to England training squad for Nations Championship
article_text:
Sale’s Joe Marchant and Gloucester’s Will Joseph are two notable inclusions among Steve Borthwick’s 36-man England squad, announced on Sunday, for the conclusion of the Nations Championship in November, with both boosting the head coach’s midfield options.

The 30-year-old centre Marchant last appeared for England at the 2023 Rugby World Cup, and spent two seasons at Stade Français in the Top 14, before returning to the Prem with Sale Sharks for this season.

Will Joseph, the 24-year-old younger brother of the former England player Jonathan Joseph, has illuminated the table-topping Gloucester’s strong start to the domestic season. He was called up by Eddie Jones for the tour to Australia in 2022, making one brief appearance off the bench in a second-Test win against the Wallabies in Brisbane.

Henry Slade, Max Ojomoh and Fraser Dingwall are Borthwick’s other centre options, with Benhard Janse van Rensburg of Bristol sidelined by a concussion sustained against Northampton this month. The Gloucester centre Charlie Atkinson is among three players called up to continue their injury rehabilitation, along with Manny Feyi-Waboso of Exeter and Bath’s Guy Pepper.

The scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet, who helped Leicester to defeat their local rivals Northampton at Welford Road on Saturday, is included along with the Saints pair of Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland.

The 21-year old McParland is uncapped, while there is no place in the squad for Ben Spencer of Bath. Kepu Tuipulotu, the Bath hooker, is another uncapped 21-year-old called up by Borthwick.

Fin Smith, Marcus Smith and George Ford are the specialist fly‑halves – while in the forwards the captain, Maro Itoje, having been rested in the summer, will return to the international stage. Alex Coles, Ollie Chessum, George Martin and Arthur Clark, another player flourishing at Gloucester, will be candidates to start with Itoje at lock. But there is no place for the 37-year-old lock Courtney Lawes, who like Marchant returned from a spell in France to sign for Sale.

Tom Pearson (Northampton) and Ben Curry (Sale) return to a squad packed with back-row talent, and will compete for starting spots with Tom Curry, Ben Earl, Henry Pollock and Greg Fisilau.

The prop Fin Baxter, who impressed for Harlequins in their victory against Saracens on Sunday, is back after almost a year sidelined with a foot injury. His clubmate Marcus Smith made a strong case to start in November by dismantling Saracens in Quins’ 33-15 win.

Borthwick’s squad assembled on Sunday at Pennyhill Park for a three‑day training camp, with the players due to return to their clubs for the Prem’s fifth round next weekend.

England begin their November programme against Australia at Twickenham on Sunday 8 November, before facing Japan on Saturday 14 November. A high-stakes encounter against the All Blacks follows on Saturday 21 November, with fixtures for the concluding Nations Championship weekend, on 27/28/29 November, to be confirmed.

title: Three-game Bledisloe Cup series looms as new deal struck
article_text:
The Wallabies will play New Zealand at the MCG in both 2027 and 2029 under a deal between Rugby Australia and the Victorian government.

There is no confirmation that the Bledisloe Cup will permanently expand to a three-game series, but the Test in 2029 will be an additional game in the series.

Next year's MCG Test in July will come ahead of the Rugby World Cup, where Australia and New Zealand will also meet in the group stage.

title: England call up star days before he qualifies for Wales | Ireland prop dies
article_text:
Here's your round-up of all the latest rugby news for the morning of Monday, October 26.

Joe Marchant has been recalled to England’s training squad for next month’s Nations Championship, two days before he could have become eligible to play for Wales.

Marchant received his first England call-up since the 2023 World Cup on Sunday night after his two-year spell at Stade Francais ended with his return to the Gallagher Prem with Sale this season, making him available for selection once again.

The 30-year-old made his last appearance in an England shirt at the 2023 Rugby World Cup, as he started in the third-place play-off clash with Argentina in Paris. Two weeks later, he made his debut for Stade Francais in the Top 14, making him ineligible for England.

Marchant becomes eligible to switch national teams on October 27, with World Rugby rules stating that captured players can change allegiances after observing a three-year stand-down period from Test rugby.

Although born in Winchester, Marchant has Welsh heritage that qualifies him to play for Wales, but that will now not be happening.

The 30-year-old is joined in the 36-man group that on Sunday begins preparations for the autumn opener against Australia by Will Joseph, the Gloucester centre whose form has lit up the Prem in the opening four rounds.

Joseph, the younger brother of former England star Jonathan Joseph, made his only Test appearance during the 2022 tour of Australia but will be looking to press his claim in the absence of Seb Atkinson.

Atkinson, who is pencilled in to start against the Wallabies at inside centre, will join the squad at their Surrey base but during this camp will be limited to rehabilitating a knee injury.

Adding to Steve Borthwick’s problems in midfield is the concussion sustained by Benhard Janse van Rensburg, who has not played since taking a head knock on club duty for Bristol on October 3.

Marchant, Joseph, Fraser Dingwall, Henry Slade and Max Ojomoh are the fit centres currently available to Borthwick.

Prop Fin Baxter makes his first appearance in an England squad since December having made a successful comeback from a foot injury in Harlequins’ Prem victory over Saracens on Sunday.

Courtney Lawes has been unable to force his way into the squad after he also joined Sale following a spell in France but could be involved later in the autumn.

Chandler Cunningham-South is missing because of an ankle problem but Ben Curry and Tom Pearson have been included as back row options.

For now Saracens’ Theo Dan has lost his place as third choice hooker behind Jamie George and Luke Cowan-Dickie with Bath’s Kepueli Tuipulotu instead given his chance to impress.

Joining Atkinson in rehabilitation are Immanuel Feyi-Waboso (hamstring) and Guy Pepper (knee).

England open the second phase of the Nations against Australia at Allianz Stadium in a fortnight before their campaign continues with fixtures against Japan and New Zealand. Finals weekend completes the month’s action.

Forwards: F Baxter (Harlequins), O Chessum (Leicester Tigers), A Clark (Gloucester Rugby), A Coles (Northampton Saints), L Cowan-Dickie (Sale Sharks), B Curry (Sale Sharks), T Curry (Sale Sharks), B Earl (Saracens), G Fisilau (Exeter Chiefs), J George (Saracens), E Genge (Bristol Bears), J Heyes (Leicester Tigers), M Itoje (Saracens), E Iyogun (Northampton Saints), G Martin (Saracens), A Opoku-Fordjour (Sale Sharks), T Pearson (Northampton Saints), H Pollock (Northampton Saints), W Stuart (Bath Rugby), K Tuipulotu (Bath Rugby).

Backs: N Caluori (Saracens), F Dingwall (Northampton Saints), G Ford (Sale Sharks), T Freeman (Northampton Saints), G Furbank (Harlequins), W Joseph (Gloucester Rugby), J Marchant (Sale Sharks), A McParland (Northampton Saints), A Mitchell (Northampton Saints), C Murley (Harlequins), M Ojomoh (Bath Rugby), H Slade (Exeter Chiefs), F Smith (Northampton Saints), M Smith (Harlequins), F Steward (Leicester Tigers), J van Poortvliet (Leicester Tigers), Rehabilitation: S Atkinson (Gloucester Rugby), I Feyi-Waboso (Exeter Chiefs), G Pepper (Bath Rugby).

Former Ireland international prop Phil O'Callaghan has passed away at the age of 83 after battling a short illness.

O'Callaghan won 21 caps for his country between 1967 and 1976, and was also part of the first Munster team to beat Australia in January 1967.

Born and raised in Cork, O'Callaghan joined local club Dolphin RFC at the age of 16, debuting in the second row.

As well as his later spells with Munster and Ireland, he also lined up for the Barbarians six times between 1969 and 1970.

After hanging up his boots, went on to coach Dolphin and Sundays Well.

He was inducted to the Munster Rugby Hall of Fame in 2016.

Scotland star Duhan van der Merwe has suffered another potential injury setback after lasting just 18 minutes on his return for Edinburgh.

The winger was making his first appearance of the season against the Lions on Friday, having returned from a long-standing ankle issue.

However, his comeback was cut short due to a hand injury.

Head coach Sean Everitt said: "Duhan got a laceration to his hand. I'm not sure what it is. I haven't been inside to chat to the medics yet."

The latest setback comes ahead of Scotland's upcoming Nations Championship campaign, with Gregor Townsend due to name his squad later today ahead of a massive clash with New Zealand on November 7.

title: Report: 15 players ‘interested’ in joining LIV Golf 2.0
article_text:
LIV Golf’s hopes of making it to 2027 have been kept alive. For now…

Fifteen players have expressed an interest in committing to LIV Golf 2.0, according to a report from the Financial Times.

While the players are unnamed, that number is enough to help the league seek a final deal over the next few days. BC Partners, the private equity firm that has pledged a $300 million bailout for LIV Golf, had put an October 25 deadline on proceedings.

BC have made clear LIV need to have “at least 30 to 40 players” committed in order to continue into a sixth season. The deadline is likely to be extended to October 30 to align with the deadline of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund which, according to the league’s bankruptcy documents, is the date it will start winding down the league as its sole lender.

The PIF has so far shelled out north of $5 billion on LIV since its inauguration in 2022.

TG has spoken to someone at LIV Golf with knowledge of the situation, who has told us there is “continued optimism here” at the league’s headquarters, and that everything regarding 2.0 remains “on schedule”.

When asked about the Financial Times report, the source described it as containing “several inaccuracies and mischaracterizations”, but added that they “will not be sharing the additional details at this time”.

They did, however, note that the number of players who have committed to LIV Golf, or remain engaged in serious, constructive discussions “is dynamic and continues to evolve”.

Sujeet Indap, who has been covering the story for the Financial Times, says interested players have been “asking BC to explain their power and governance rights in LIV 2.0” – with particular focus on how the league will generate income as well as any particular risks for the golfers.

The report also notes that 23 players are still locked in legal talks with LIV and the PIF over money still owed. Jon Rahm, who signed for a reported $450m at the start of the 2023 season, won more money than any other player in LIV’s five years to date, but was forced to leave a large amount on the table in order to break free from his contract.

Rahm’s fellow team captains, Louis Oosthuizen and Ian Poulter, have also declared themselves out of LIV, as have the Spaniard’s Legion XIII colleagues Tyrrell Hatton and Tom McKibbin as players continue to either quit or signal their intentions to quit.

So far, only five players – Richard Bland, Cameron Tringale, Brendan Steele, Victor Perez and Ben Campbell – have publicly stated that they would like to remain a part of LIV 2.0, though it is unknown how many of them are part of the 15 reported by the Financial Times. The biggest name yet to commit either way is Bryson DeChambeau, who continues to leave question marks over his future.

Meanwhile, Dustin Johnson is leading a group of players, while also includes Bubba Watson, in seeking severance payments from the PIF after “career-altering decisions” were made based on promises that have not been kept.

title: Soccer sponsorships: Chelsea, Marseille, Valencia
article_text:
English and French soccer heavyweights Chelsea and Olympique de Marseille have both unveiled significant new sponsorship deals.

English Premier League side Chelsea have brought in worldwide payments and financial platform Sokin as a new sleeve sponsor, in a multi-year deal, while Ligue 1's Marseille have announced similar global money transfer app Sendwave as a new premium partner.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Through the latter agreement, Sendwave, part of the Zepz group, will benefit from visibility on the lower backs of the Marseille team kit in all 2026-27 Ligue 1 games.

Stéphane Richard, Olympique de Marseille president, commented: "The arrival of a new international player by our side is an important show of confidence in the club. It confirms our ability to attract international companies that wish to support our development and back the team."

The Chelsea-Sokin deal, meanwhile, sees that brand – aside from the primary sleeve sponsorship element – become a principal partner of London club Chelsea, as well as the club's official business payments and FX partner. The deal covers both the men's and women's sides.

The Sokin logo will be covered on the sleeves of all kits worn by the men's, women's, and academy Chelsea sides, during matches, across the length of the tie-up.

That logo adorned the men's team's sleeves for the first time during Chelsea's 0-2 home loss to London rivals Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday.

Vroon Modgill, Sokin's chief executive and founder, commented: "Chelsea plays on the biggest stage in world football, and its business runs in dozens of currencies. Sokin was built for that with regulated, multi-currency payments and foreign exchange for organisations that operate internationally."

The most prominent move from Sokin – recently – in the sports sponsorship space saw the company brought in as the inaugural shirt sponsor for MI London, one of the teams from English domestic cricket's short-form The Hundred competition.

In terms of recent Chelsea commercial agreements, the West London club brought in global automotive brand GAC as a sponsor in early October.

Chelsea have also expanded their existing agreement with Fanatics-owned collectables brand Topps recently.

Chelsea currently sit fifth in the 20-team Premier League, after eight matches. Marseille, meanwhile, lie eighth in the 18-team Ligue 1.

Elsewhere in European soccer, troubled Spanish side Valencia have struck a two-season tie-up with fashion brand Scalpers.

A deal between those two parties was unveiled late last week, stretching across the 2026-27 and 2027-28 campaigns.

The agreement entails that the brand outfitting club players and staff with specifically-designed collections during the length of the deal.

The Scalpers collection for Valencia is now on sale.

Peter Lim, the unpopular owner of Valencia, confirmed late last week that a 42% stake has been sold to an investment group backed by the co-founders of the KKR private equity investment group.

The consortium taking over that sizeable minority stake is called Pitchwise Holdings.

title: First Scotland call-up for Newcastle's Leatherbarrow
article_text:
Uncapped Newcastle Red Bulls back row Ollie Leatherbarrow has been called up by Scotland for the first time for the three home Nations Championship fixtures against New Zealand, Australia and Japan.

But in-form Edinburgh forwards Magnus Bradbury and Freddy Douglas are surprising omissions from the 37-strong squad.

Macclesfield-born Leatherbarrow qualifies for Scotland because of his grandmother being from Perth and has already represented Scotland at under-16 and under-20 levels.

The 24-year-old began his career at Exeter Chiefs before moving to Newcastle in 2023. Senior trio Jamie Ritchie, Darcy Graham and Duhan van der Merwe have all been included after returning recently from injuries.

"This has been my goal for a long time," Leatherbarrow said. "When you feel like you are playing well for your club, you're obviously looking to get that national call-up.

"It's just about showing what I can do. My strength is probably ball-carrying, so that lends itself to number eight a bit more, but I'm probably more the size of a seven.

"I've played all three back row positions for Newcastle and I'm happy to play wherever really."

Head coach Gregor Townsend acknowledged Bradbury's strong start to the season but said he was "looking for more" from the 31-year-old.

"We know Magnus is hugely motivated for Scotland," he explained. "We know the qualities he brings.

"We're also aware that Jack Dempsey [now based in Japan] is not going to be available in the Six Nations, so it's an opportunity for us to look at someone else in our environment.

"We know Ollie can cover all three positions in the back row. He's an openside by trade, but he's played a lot of rugby at six and eight.

"He'll be challenging for a place now and in the Six Nations, like Magnus will be as well."

Glasgow Warriors' Seb Stephen, who made his debut in July's Nations Championship match against Fiji, is one of three hookers selected.

Experienced Edinburgh lock Grant Gilchrist is not included after returning from injury, while club-mate Hector Patterson had been touted for potential involvement after a bright start to the season, but the scrum-half has not made the cut.

Townsend said no decision has been made yet on New Zealand-born Josh McKay, the 29-year-old Glasgow full-back who will be eligible in time for the final Test against Japan.

Scotland host the All Blacks on 7 November, the Wallabies on 15 November and the Brave Blossoms on 21 November at Murrayfield before the new Nations Championship concludes the following weekend at Twickenham, based around final hemisphere positions.

The finals are on the weekend of 28-29 November, with fixtures determined by the placings of northern and southern hemisphere countries across these games and the ones played in July.

Forwards: Ewan Ashman (Edinburgh), Josh Bayliss (Bath), Gregor Brown, Scott Cummings, Alex Craig, Rory Darge (all Glasgow Warriors), Jack Dempsey (Toshiba Brave Lupus), Matt Fagerson, Zander Fagerson (both Glasgow Warriors), Jonny Gray (Perpignan), Gregor Hiddleston (Glasgow Warriors), Will Hurd (Leicester Tigers), Ollie Leatherbarrow (Newcastle Red Bulls), Nathan McBeth (Glasgow Warriors), Liam McConnell (Edinburgh), Elliot Millar Mills (Newcastle Red Bulls), Jamie Ritchie (Glasgow Warriors), Pierre Schoeman (Edinburgh), Rory Sutherland, Seb Stephen, Max Williamson (all Glasgow Warriors).

Backs: Fergus Burke (Saracens), Jamie Dobie (Glasgow Warriors), Darcy Graham (Edinburgh), George Horne (Glasgow Warriors), Rory Hutchinson (Northampton Saints), Huw Jones (Toulon), Tom Jordan (Bristol Bears), Blair Kinghorn (Toulouse), Stafford McDowall, Kyle Rowe (both Glasgow Warriors), Finn Russell (Bath), Ollie Smith, Kyle Steyn, Sione Tuipulotu, capt (all Glasgow Warriors), Duhan van der Merwe (Edinburgh), Ben White (Toulon).

title: France revise squad for Nations Championship as Top 14 casualties mount
article_text:
Two weeks out from the start of next month’s Nations Championship, Fabien Galthié has been forced to make four changes to the Les Bleus squad after injuries to Section Paloise’s Fabien Brau-Boirie, Stade Rochelais’ Antoine Hastoy and Karl Sorin, and Union Bordeaux Bègles’ Marko Gazzotti.

The four were the latest injury victims following another intense round in the Top 14, prompting France’s head coach to call up UBB’s Nicolas Depoortère, Castres Louis Le Brun, Section Paloise’s Thomas Laclayat and Stade Toulousain’s Anthony Jelonch as replacements.

Among the reported injuries, Fabien Brau-Boirie’s is the most concerning; the centre left the field clutching his knee and is now awaiting further examinations to confirm the extent of the damage.

The reigning Six Nations champions had already been hit by a wave of injuries to key players; notably, Matthieu Jalibert, Thomas Ramos, and Demba Bamba were ruled out from November with serious injuries that will keep them sidelined until late December.

Jalibert, who played a vital role in the Six Nations and the July window of the Nations Championship, sustained an injury on 20 September when UBB faced Stade Français, with the fly-half coming off 14 minutes into the game.

As for the new faces, Castres fly-half Louis Le Brun is one of the players yet to earn a cap for France.

Depoortère was in the July travelling squad but made only a 14-minute cameo against the All Blacks before missing out on the next two games. The Bordeaux centre now has another chance to earn Galthié’s trust one year from the Rugby World Cup.

Concerning Jelonch, the back-rower, had started in four of France’s five Six Nations matches, but following a below-par performance against Scotland, he was dropped from the squad and ultimately missed the tour to the Southern Hemisphere and Japan in July.

Finally, prop Thomas Laclayat hasn’t been called up to the French national team since November 2025; he now has the chance to add to his three caps.

France will host Fiji on the opening weekend of July, then face the four-time World Champions, South Africa, on the 14th, before wrapping up the pool stages of the Nations Championship against Argentina on the 21st.

They currently lead the Northern Hemisphere pool with 12 points, and despite the absences they have had to deal with, Galthié’s goal is to reach the final of the competition in its debut year.

title: Smotherman beats Power in Monday finish in Bermuda
article_text:
Austin Smotherman claimed his second PGA Tour title with a Monday play-off victory over Seamus Power at the weather-hit Bermuda Championship.

The 32-year-old American parred the third extra hole to fend off the Irishman and seal his second tournament win in as many starts after a breakthrough victory in Utah earlier this month.

Smotherman and Power contested the sudden-death play-off on Monday after inclement weather forced organisers to cancel Sunday's scheduled final round.

With more bad weather forecast on Monday, officials decided to scrap the final round and proceed with a play-off between the 54-hole leaders.

Smotherman carded 65, 66 and 66 to reach 16 under through three rounds, with 2022 champion Power matching his 197 total with rounds of 66, 64 and 67.

On the first play-off hole - the par-three 16th at Port Royal Golf Course - Power missed a 20-footer for his third PGA Tour win before getting up and down from the bunker to force a third extra hole.

With the hole location having been changed, Smotherman two-putted from 15 feet for the win after Power failed to get up and down for par from the rough.

"We're out here playing an incredible sport in a beautiful spot," said Smotherman.

"Whatever things are going to be thrown at us, Zak [Williamson, caddie] and I were going to be on top of our game.

"Yesterday I felt like we handled everything pretty well and the tour has been great at communicating what's going to happen today for us.

"Once we got that news, it was nice to know what's going on. To come out on top is a cherry on top, so it's pretty awesome."

While Power missed out on the trophy, the runner-up finish effectively guarantees his PGA Tour card for 2027 after playing with conditional status this year.

Having entered the week 103rd in the FedEx Cup Fall standings, the 39-year-old is projected to climb to 53rd, with the top 100 earning PGA Tour cards for next year.

"Had a chance this morning, wasn't able to do it, which is disappointing, but overall great week, can't complain too much," said Power.

"Hit some good shots in the playoff, just didn't quite judge the wind right, but that's golf sometimes. I'll move onwards."

title: New WRU chair prepared to abandon axe plan as he refuses to be a 'yes man'
article_text:
The new Welsh Rugby Union chair, Lyndon Faulkner, has vowed he will not be a “yes man" and insisted he will recommend abandoning plans to cut Welsh rugby to three professional teams if a review of the evidence convinces him it is the wrong decision for the game.

Faulkner, who is due to take up the role at the end of November, says he would not have accepted the job if he had been expected to rubber-stamp decisions already made by the governing body.

The WRU is currently set to reduce Wales’ professional rugby landscape from four teams to three, leaving either the Ospreys or Scarlets facing the prospect of being cut. The proposals also include investing £28m in the pathway over the next five years.

Faulkner has yet to reveal how many professional teams he believes Wales can sustain, but is prepared to review all the available data before making a decision.

"So, here's my plan," he told WalesOnline in his first major interview. "First of all, I'm not in the job yet and officially I'm not in the job until the end of November.

"What I am going to do is start on November 2 and I am going to be looking at everything.

"There's some talk out there that whoever took this job was under the condition they can't talk about the four to three or four to two or whatever it is going to be.

"That is absolutely incorrect. I wouldn't have taken the job with those conditions.

"So, I feel it's my job to look at everything we've got going on, challenge it, probe it and hopefully bring my experience to bear where I think we can do things better."

Faulkner is also willing to recommend a change of course for the WRU if he believes that is the right way forward.

"Yes and that's on anything I see," said Faulkner when asked if he was prepared to force change.

"Whatever I feel I see, I will make my case. I haven't done what I've done in business by not doing that.

"To the extent I'll see change then I will be making recommendations.

"Of course I'll be making recommendations to change whatever that might be."

Faulkner's credentials are formidable. He played key roles in the introduction of CDs and DVDs, helped bring Xbox, Windows XP and Office 2000 to market during his time at Microsoft, and oversaw the flotation of Nimbus CD International on Nasdaq.

Subsequent acquisitions helped transform Technicolor into a global player in digital media and home entertainment.

Faulkner was also at the forefront of the compact disc revolution, championing the technology when the music industry remained wedded to vinyl and cassette.

At Nimbus, he secured the backing of Richard Branson before taking the technology to America. Following Robert Maxwell’s acquisition of the company, Faulkner led a management buyout after Maxwell’s death.

His record at Pelican Products, where he held senior leadership roles between 2006 and 2021, was similarly impressive.

Faulkner is candid about the qualities that have underpinned his success, insisting he would not have reached the heights he has in business had he been a yes man or lacked the ruthlessness required to make tough decisions.

"I wouldn't have taken the job were it to be me needing to be a yes man," he said.

"Look at my resume and my CV. Also, just so you know everything, I've probed on everything and I'm starting to ask for information.

"The information is coming. Nobody is holding anything back from me. I'm not getting anything that's filtered.

"I'm getting stuff on finance and stuff like that as I prepare to look at things fully disclosed.

"Everyone is sending me everything I'm asking for. I say that as a point of reference as well.

"Many people have asked me why I've taken this job?

"Let's be honest, I'm putting my professional reputation on the line.

"It's impeccable to date. I batted six for six. So yes there is reputational risk for me but there's no financial risk.

"I don't need the job. This is purely motivated around trying to help and make a difference for Welsh rugby to be better."

Faulkner will join a 12-strong WRU board whose members have all backed the current proposals, including cutting one professional team in west Wales and investing £28m in the pathway over the next five years.

The chairman has traditionally wielded considerable influence within the boardroom, giving Faulkner a significant voice in determining the future direction of Welsh rugby.

While his role is non-executive, Faulkner has made clear that his appointment must mean his experience and recommendations are taken seriously.

"Let's be perfectly clear, this is a non-executive role," he said.

"I'm not running the organisation but I am the chair and have the experience, that's why they picked me because of my experience.

"It would be foolish to pick me and then not take consideration of what I say.

"It depends on the severity of the nature. If it's a light item we could agree to disagree and perhaps we all move on as normal.

"If it's something that's relevant and they don't agree then probably I'm not the man for the job."

While Faulkner is open to changing course, he is also a decisive operator who will not shy away from pushing through unpopular reforms if he believes they are in the best long-term interests of Welsh rugby. That means if he believes the WRU's current course is the right one, he won't bow to the public pressure currently being applied from multiple directions.

title: Tour winners take aim at LIV Golf stars over ‘hilarious’ U-turn
article_text:
Among the many consequences of the ongoing exodus at LIV Golf is the sense of resentment that will soon linger on driving ranges across Europe.

As LIV stars finalise plans to use the DP World Tour as a landing ground after declining the chance to help relaunch the next iteration of the beleaguered league, the circuit’s current membership are beginning to voice their frustrations.

“Four years ago they didn’t give a s**t about the DP World Tour,” six-time winner Joost Luiten told TG earlier this month. “They made a decision to go after the money. And now all of a sudden, the money is gone and they want to come back and act like nothing happened. I don’t think that’s right.”

Luiten’s sentiment is shared by some of his fellow members.

Ewen Ferguson’s ire lies with the players who apparently showed no contrition or gratitude to his circuit when signing for the breakaway league.

“I have to say, some of the Liv players coming back to play DP is actually cool as some really good players,” the three-time DP World Tour champion wrote on X, “but hilarious how some of them slammed the tour for so long, not one good thing to say about it, now it’s the best thing since sliced bread and feels like coming home.”

Richard Mansell, another DP World Tour winner, concurs.

“Spot on my mate,” he wrote. “I haven’t been around the tour a lot this year and when I have since coming back from injury my golf hasn’t been where I want it so I don’t want to say too much. However, things are going to look different in 2027. Some should be allowed back and some shouldn’t.”

Three-time winner Marco Penge added: “Well said, it’s pretty simple. I think the reason for leaving the DP World Tour to go to LIV kind of speaks for itself.”

The complexities of the subject of LIV players seeking arrangements with Wentworth officials was brought into sharp focus by Eddie Pepperell last week. The Englishman, one of several prominent names to lose his full DP World Tour card after the Genesis Championship in Korea, wrote a thoughtful column about the issue for The Chipping Forecast.

“As someone who has gone through the wringer this game provides, and who has gone back to Q School and had two immensely divergent experiences, betrayal feels like the right word,” Pepperell wrote. “And unfortunately loss of respect, resentment and contempt. I don’t want to feel resentment or contempt towards the DPWT, but I’m afraid it is an inevitability and I most probably won’t be the only one.”

Lee Westwood has yet to publicly declare his intentions for next season, but would be free to join the DP World Tour next season based on an exemption category after settling fines with his old domain.

Westwood weighed on X, arguing the DP World Tour finds itself in an “interesting position” and is “caught between needing ‘names’ at those times of year when they don’t get strong fields [in] January to June, giving invites to people who have shown no interest in the tour other than now when they’ve nowhere else to play, and keeping the members happy that support the tour at the smaller events and the lads that have gone through all the qualifying stages.

“Anyone with an exemption should be free to come back because as we know the DPWT endorses members going to another rival tour and already have 10 cards for it but if people don’t have an exemption they should have to go through the school like everyone else.”

It is not entirely clear how many LIV players will be welcomed back to the DP World Tour next season, but TG revealed this month that several of them are in talks over a deal that will guarantee a specific number of tournament invites, on the condition they don’t sign up to LIV 2.0.

Some LIV stars will leave and sign contracts to play a certain number of DP World Tour events, despite having no previous status. The circuit is attempting to manage a delicate situation by extracting value from LIV players without denying opportunities to current members.

title: All to Play For: Yuto Katsuragawa seals Play-Off spot with Korea victory
article_text:
Yuto Katsuragawa is heading to the DP World Tour Play-Offs after turning his season upside down with victory at Genesis Championship.

The Japanese entered the week at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club 106th in the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World and battling to break the top 100 and keep full playing privileges for next season.

He produced when it mattered most, however, with a blistering 63 on day three catapulting him into a two-shot lead that he would not relinquish despite a closing 71.

The 835.00 points for victory jumped him 78 places in the Rankings to 28th and he will now be heading to both the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship and the season-ending DP World Tour Championship.

It is a remarkable turnaround for a player who made just three DP World Tour cuts in 2024 after winning the ISPS HANDA - CHAMPIONSHIP and finished 91st on the Rankings last term in large part thanks to a top ten at the regular-season ending event in Korea.

The 2026 season had brought just one top ten before he returned to the peninsula but he is now back in Category 3 as a winner.

"After the first win, I had such a hard time, struggling with that time, but having the second win, this is definitely the greatest moment of my life," he said.

"Yes I was nervous, not just for the victory but also about the seed for the DP World Tour so it was double nervous for me but I think I got through.

"I had a good image from the first victory, I just kept that good feeling about it and I came for the second win.

"I'm very happy because to play on the DP World Tour is something I need in my life and I am very happy to play in Dubai."

The top 70 available players after the week in Korea were guaranteed a spot in the Play-Offs and Frederic Lacroix and Antoine Rozner both cracked the top 70 after finishing in ties for second and fourth respectively.

Sean Crocker was the other big winner in the Rankings last week as he birdied his last four holes in a back nine of 29 on Sunday to finish in a tie for 34th and move up three spots into 100th.

title: PGA of America name 2029 Ryder Cup championship director: "The opportunity of a lifetime"
article_text:
The PGA of America have announced Laura Frick will be the championship director of the 2029 Ryder Cup.

Frick will oversee on-site operations for the biennial contest between the United States and Europe, which will return to Hazeltine for the first time since 2016.

The PGA has confirmed to GolfMagic that Frick now becomes their second female overall to be championship director for the Ryder Cup.

Tara Guenthner oversaw the 2008 Ryder Cup at Valhalla.

Frick is the first female PGA of America Golf Professional to hold the title.

The appointment marks another significant milestone in Frick’s career after she became the first female PGA of America Golf professional to serve as championship director at the 2026 KPMG Women's PGA Championship, which was also held at the Minnesota venue.

"I'm proud of the dedication it took to get here and I'm so thankful for the network of people who guided and supported me along the way," Frick told the official PGA website.

She added: "It's truly a job that I will look forward to waking up for every day.”

Frick joined the PGA of America after graduating from Ferris State University in 2015, having studied on its PGA Golf Management programme.

She initially worked in the organisation's player engagement and member championships departments before becoming director of competitions in December 2021.

In that position, she led national events including the PGA Jr. League Championships and managed programmes designed to increase participation in the sport.

Her experience coordinating major events, working with stakeholders and overseeing tournament operations is expected to be central to preparations for the 2029 Ryder Cup.

Hazeltine has an established history of hosting elite golf, having staged the Ryder Cup in 2016, when the United States defeated Europe 17-11 to reclaim the trophy after three consecutive European victories.

Hazeltine will become the first American course to host the Ryder Cup twice when the competition returns in 2029.

The event will follow the 2027 Ryder Cup at Adare Manor in County Limerick, Ireland, as the United States and Europe continue their long-running contest.

Europe will be attempting to win the Ryder Cup three times in a row for the first time since 2014.

Frick's appointment builds on her role at the 2026 KPMG Women's PGA Championship and places her at the centre of preparations for one of the biggest events on the international golf calendar.

title: Sky Sports launches WSL series with Ella Toone and Keely Hodgkinson
article_text:
Sky Sports has launched Minus 1, a new digital series offering a behind-the-scenes look at the lives of Women’s Super League players, with Manchester United midfielder Ella Toone and Olympic 800m champion Keely Hodgkinson featuring in the opening episode.

The series is designed to bring fans closer to WSL players beyond matchday coverage, combining conversations about football with insights into their personalities, friendships and interests away from the pitch.

The first episode brings together Toone and Hodgkinson ahead of the Manchester derby, following the two friends as they spend time at Manchester United’s training ground and discuss their experiences of elite sport.

The programme also explores the preparation and routines involved in competing at the highest level, offering a different perspective on two of Britain’s most recognisable female athletes.

Further episodes will feature WSL players alongside guests from sport and popular culture, with content distributed across Sky Sports’ digital and social channels, including its dedicated WSL TikTok account.

The launch adds to Sky Sports’ investment in women’s football content beyond live broadcasting. The broadcaster holds rights to approximately 90% of Women’s Super League matches, giving it a significant role in how the competition reaches UK audiences.

Through Minus 1, Sky is seeking to build on that coverage by creating short-form, personality-led programming that can reach viewers who may not regularly watch live matches.

The opening episode also draws on the crossover appeal of Toone and Hodgkinson, whose friendship connects two of Britain’s leading women’s sports.

The format gives Sky Sports another opportunity to develop the visibility of WSL players while expanding its digital offering around the competition.

title: Southampton FC extend 25-year partnership with Peter Cooper Motor Group
article_text:
Southampton FC have renewed their partnership with Peter Cooper Motor Group for the 2026/27 season, extending a commercial relationship that has lasted more than 25 years.

The family-owned automotive retailer will continue as a Regional Partner of the Championship club, while maintaining its support for Saints Foundation as a patron for a sixth consecutive year.

The agreement continues one of Southampton’s longest-standing local commercial relationships, with the motor group involved in fan engagement activities, player challenges and community initiatives throughout its association with the club.

Under the renewed arrangement, Peter Cooper Motor Group will continue supporting club activities aimed at engaging supporters, alongside the Foundation’s work across Southampton and the surrounding region.

The business has operated in the area for decades, building its automotive retail presence through its longstanding association with Volkswagen and a portfolio that now includes Kia, Jaecoo, Omoda, Jeep and Xpeng.

Phil Parsons, CEO of Southampton FC, said, “We’re delighted that Peter Cooper Motor Group are continuing as a partner of Southampton Football Club. As a business with strong roots in the local community, they share our commitment to the region and the people who make it special. Partnerships like this are important to the growth of the club, and we look forward to continuing a successful relationship with the team at Peter Cooper Motor Group, working together to create value for both our organisations and our supporters.”

The renewal also extends the motor group’s relationship with Saints Foundation, the club’s charitable organisation, which delivers community programmes across the region.

Darren Cooper, Managing Director of Peter Cooper Motor Group, said, “We’re incredibly proud to be renewing our partnership with Southampton Football Club and to continue a relationship that has been such an important part of our business for more than 20 years.

“Southampton FC is at the heart of the local community, and our shared commitment to the city and its people makes this partnership particularly special. It gives us the opportunity to connect with supporters, get involved in exciting club initiatives and play our part in supporting the wider community.

“We’re also delighted to continue our support for Saints Foundation for a sixth consecutive year. The work it does to improve lives and create opportunities for people across the region is hugely valuable, and we’re proud to be able to support its ongoing mission.”

title: Double World Cup winner Kwagga Smith signs for the Bulls
article_text:
Springbok back-rower Kwagga Smith, 33, will likely see out the remainder of his career at the Bulls after signing a three-year deal with the Pretoria-based team.

Smith’s signature has long been rumoured and now the Bulls have confirmed the versatile double World Cup winner is joining them.

Bulls coach Johan Ackermann said he was delighted to team up again with Smith, having coached him previously at the Lions.

“As a youngster, he showed character and fight and integrity. He’s a team man who has grown into a stalwart, and it’s been a privilege to watch his career unfold and establish himself as one of the best backrows in world rugby. Wherever he goes he makes a difference, and I look forward to him contributing both on and off the field.”

Smith made his name in sevens, winning gold in the Commonwealth Games in 2014 before adding an Olympic bronze medal to his collection in 2016.

In 15s, his first big break came at the Lions, where he was part of the side that won the 2015 Currie Cup. He then moved to Japan in 2018 and has spent eight years there with Yamaha Júbilo, now rebranded as the Shizuoka Blue Revs.

During that time, he was a Springbok regular and has amassed 63 caps to date, winning a host of honours along the way.

In addition to the 2019 and 2023 World Cup wins, Smith featured in the 2021 series win over the British & Irish Lions, and the Rugby Championship titles of 2019, 2024 and 2025.

He tore his ACL and meniscus in May while playing for the Blue Revs, but has been cleared to play at the end of December.

“I’m very excited to be joining,” said Smith, who mentioned that he was tracking well with his recovery.

“I’m already jogging. I miss the rugby but I’m feeling good.

“My wife is pregnant, due in January, so the timing of joining the Vodacom Bulls is perfect.

“Playing under Johan Ackermann [previously] was one of my best experiences. I’m looking forward to getting back by early next year.”

title: Handre Pollard is the latest Springbok added to Bulls' injury list
article_text:
The Bulls are waiting on the results of scan to see if Handre Pollard will be available for their next United Rugby Championship fixture against the struggling Scarlets.

Pollard sustained a hamstring injury in the Bulls’ 34-26 URC victory over Ulster and his fitness will be confirmed once the results have been assessed.

Meanwhile, the URC’s third-placed team have provided updates on fellow Boks, wing/centre Canan Moodie and scrum-half Embrose Papier.

Moodie has returned to training under the Head Injury Assessment (HIA) return-to-play protocols. He will not be considered for selection this week, while Papier is recovering from an ankle operation and will be out for several weeks.

In other related injury news, the Bulls have confirmed that wing Cheswill Jooste has undergone an operation for a broken cheekbone. After suffering a head injury against Ulster, the speedster faces a mandatory two-week stand-down period under HIA protocols, and extended rest has been recommended.

Centre Sango Xamlashe will not be considered for selection this week after he completed HIA protocols following a concussion in Saturday’s match, while wing Thakir Abrahams is not expected to be sidelined with a hamsting injury for more than a week.

title: Eddie Jones goes rogue in fly-half picks for Nations Championship
article_text:
Deprived of more experienced options at 10, Eddie Jones has picked two fly-halves with three caps between for them for Japan’s Northern Hemipshere tour in the Nations Championship.

Seungsin Lee was the leading points scorer in world rugby in 2025, and had been the regular pick at 10 for a couple of seasons until suffering an injury in Kobelco Kobe Steelers’ 22-13 win over Kubota Spears in the Japanese Rugby League One Championship final in May.

Ryunosuke Ito was thrown in at the deep end for the Southern Hemisphere Series of the Nations Championship in July and came through his first-ever game of professional rugby, the 27-10 win over Italy, with flying colours.

The fourth-year university student, 21, has started every Test since then, but will not be available for the Brave Blossoms in November, as he is due to play for Meiji University in the Kanto University Intercollegiate Championship.

Meanwhile, Jones has resisted calls to select Kobe Steelers full-back Shunsuke Uenobo and Black Rams Tokyo playmaker Ichigo Nakakusu for the games against Wales, England and Scotland.

Never afraid to blood new talent – Japan handed debuts to more players than any other leading nation in 2025 (23), Jones has instead put his faith in Honda Heat’s uncapped fly-half Riku Kitahara.

Kitahara will compete with Toyota’s Shinya Komura, who won the last of his three caps as a replacement against Georgia in November last year.

Jones’ 35-man roster includes a total of three Test rookies, with Kitahara joined by Riku Tokita in the backs and Miu Austin Moriyama in the forwards. Japan selected 13 uncapped players in their squad for the Southern Hemisphere Series.

title: Fit-again Lions duo return to Scotland squad for Nations Championship
article_text:
Blair Kinghorn and Huw Jones are ready to pull on a Scotland jersey again for the first time since the Guinness Six Nations after being named in Gregor Townsend’s Nations Championship squad for November.

The celebrated duo, with 131 caps between them, were given the summer off and have recently overcome knocks to be considered for selection for the Murrayfield Tests against New Zealand (7 November), Australia (15 November) and Japan (21 November).

Senior trio Jamie Ritchie, Darcy Graham and Duhan van der Merwe have also been included after returning recently from injuries.

Glasgow hooker Seb Stephen, who made his debut in the summer, has kept his place alongside other recent additions to the forward pack, Liam McConnell and Gregor Hiddleston.

Influential back-rower Jack Dempsey has retained his place despite leaving Glasgow in the summer to move to Japan.

Experienced lock Grant Gilchrist – who recently returned from injury – is a notable absentee from the squad, while Hector Patterson had been touted for potential involvement after a bright start to the season but the Edinburgh scrum-half has not made the cut.

Sione Tuipulotu leads the 37-strong group, which includes uncapped Newcastle back-row forward Ollie Leatherbarrow. The 24-year-old qualifies for Scotland through his Perth-born grandmother.

Leatherbarrow began his career at Exeter Chiefs before moving to Newcastle Red Bulls in 2023 and has previously represented Scotland at U16 and U20 level.

Scrum-half George Horne will reach 50 caps for Scotland if he features in all three Tests.

title: British teenager Klugman wins Wrexham Open title
article_text:
British teenager Hannah Klugman won the biggest title of her career with an impressive performance against Elsa Jacquemot in the final of the Lexus Wrexham Open.

The 17-year-old defeated her French opponent 6-2 6-4 to clinch the W100 title without dropping a set all week.

She becomes the second successive British player to win the Wrexham title after Wales' Mimi Xu last year, and is the youngest Briton to win a singles trophy at W100 level or higher.

Klugman pressed the world number 157 straight from the first game. Despite missing her first two break-point opportunities, she got her reward just two games later.

A double break for the Briton sealed an emphatic first set, and she picked up where she left off in the second, racing to a 5-1 lead.

In the biggest match of her career so far, Klugman had to fight to get over the line. Jacquemot got back to 5-4 before the home favourite served out the victory at the second time of asking.

"I was shaking afterwards, but just so, so happy and proud of myself again," said Klugman.

"It's been such an amazing week and to top it off with a win at such a high-level tournament, these are big moments for me as a young player."

More British success followed as Freya Christie and Eden Silva beat Japan's Hiroko Kuwata and India's Ankita Raina 6-2 6-3 in the doubles final.

title: Agency scores county cricket sponsorship deal
article_text:
A sports agency has added another innings to its portfolio with a cricketing deal.

Sporting Group International is working with Glamorgan County Cricket Club.

Bosses say the firm will help the Welsh outfit secure first-team kit sponsorship for next season’s domestic campaign.

The partnership also covers The Hundred competition, where the Cardiff-based club has a stake in the Welsh Fire franchise alongside US tech entrepreneur Sanjay Govil.

Adrian Wright, group chief executive at Birmingham-based Sporting Group International, said: “We are delighted to be working with Glamorgan to help it secure a principal partner for the club and its assets across The Hundred and domestic cricket next summer.”

Ian Davis, Glamorgan head of partnership sales, added: “We are sure Sporting Group International will help us attract a strong brand that is keen on the international exposure both Glamorgan County Cricket Club and Welsh Fire can offer.”

The work comes after Sporting Group International landed three sponsorship deals for Gloucestershire County Cricket Club, which included electric vehicle charging firm Easee acting as front-of-shirt sponsor for the side’s men’s and women’s Metro Bank One Day Cup 2026 teams.

It also previously unveiled a Professional Darts Corporation venture to secure a sponsor for the game’s 170 ‘Big Fish’ checkout, and a partnership with Hartlepool United Football Club to source sponsors across its first-team kit, naming rights and digital channels.

title: World Rugby reveals Women's 15s Player, Breakthrough Player and Try of the Year nominees for 2026
article_text:
Eight outstanding players from six nations have been shortlisted in recognition of their exceptional performances and impact throughout the international season, reflecting the depth of talent and growing competitiveness of the women's game.

The winners of both awards will be revealed this weekend, with trophies presented following the players' final WXV Global Series matches.

The announcement also marks the opening of the fan vote for the IRPA Women's 15s Try of the Year 2026, with four memorable tries shortlisted by the International Rugby Players' Association and supporters around the world invited to select the winner.

Since their inception in 2001, the World Rugby Awards have recognised and celebrated achievements at the highest level of the game, honouring the players and individuals whose exceptional performances, dedication and contributions embody the values of rugby.

The Women's 15s Player of the Year remains one of the most prestigious individual honours in the sport. Four outstanding internationals have been shortlisted following exceptional performances throughout the 2026 season.

A commanding presence at fly-half, Harrison has been instrumental in directing England's attack with her game management, tactical kicking and ability to deliver in decisive moments. Her match-winning interception try against New Zealand in September underlined her composure and influence in the biggest contests.

A key figure in the Red Roses' backline, Jones has continued to demonstrate her versatility, attacking threat and defensive qualities throughout 2026. Equally influential with and without the ball, the experienced centre has also taken on the captaincy of the world champions.

A cornerstone of Canada's forward pack, Menin has continued to impress with her physicality, powerful scrummaging and tireless work around the field. The experienced tight-head prop has been a key figure in Canada's front row, providing a strong platform for her team's performances against the world's leading nations.

A dynamic presence in the Black Ferns' back row, Olsen-Baker has showcased her powerful ball-carrying, athleticism and relentless work-rate throughout the year. Her ability to make an impact on both sides of the ball has made her an important figure in New Zealand's forward pack.

In addition to the final shortlist, the selection panel recognised several players whose standout performances throughout 2026 warranted special commendation in Ireland hooker Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald, New Zealand tight-head prop Veisinia Mahutariki-Fakalelu and openside flanker Elinor-Plum King.

The Women's 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year award celebrates emerging talents who have made an outstanding impact on the international stage in their debut year and demonstrated their potential to shape the future of the game.

This year's shortlist features four exciting players representing Australia, France, New Zealand and USA, highlighting the next generation of talent across the global women's game.

An exciting emerging talent in French rugby, Barrat has made a strong impression with her attacking instincts and confident performances on the international stage. Named Women's Six Nations Breakthrough Player of the Tournament in 2026, she has quickly established herself as one of France's most promising young players.

An impressive addition to the Black Ferns' forward pack, King has caught the eye with her physicality, defensive work and presence at the breakdown. The openside flanker has shown maturity beyond her experience, establishing herself as an exciting prospect in New Zealand's back row.

An exciting attacking talent, Whitaker has made her mark on the international stage with her pace, finishing ability and willingness to take on defenders. The Wallaroos winger has continued to grow in confidence throughout the WXV Global Series, including crossing for a try against Scotland.

One of the emerging talents for the Women’s Eagles, Vogel has earned recognition for her performances on the international stage in 2026. Her inclusion on the shortlist reflects her growing influence and potential as part of the next generation of American rugby talent.

Four unforgettable tries have been shortlisted for the IRPA Women's 15s Try of the Year 2026, with rugby fans around the world invited to decide the winner.

Selected by the International Rugby Players' Association, the nominations celebrate the attacking flair, creativity and skill on display across the international women's game this season.

World Rugby Chair Brett Robinson said: “The quality of this year's nominees is a testament to the incredible talent, dedication and ambition driving women's rugby forward. From established international stars to exciting emerging players, each has made an outstanding contribution to the game in 2026.

“As women's rugby continues to grow and reach new audiences around the world, it is important that we recognise the players whose performances inspire fans and the next generation. I congratulate all our nominees on their achievements and look forward to celebrating the very best of our sport through this year's awards.”

Fans will have the opportunity to vote on social media to determine the winner of Try of the Year, with voting opening on Monday, 26 October and closing on Wednesday, 28 October.

The celebrations will conclude on Monday 2 November, with the unveiling of the World Rugby Women's 15s Dream Team of the Year, recognising the outstanding performers who have defined the international season.

title: Djokovic Returns to Basel, Targeting Turin
article_text:
Novak Djokovic is back in Basel for the first time since 2011, as the 24-time Grand Slam champion and owner of 102 ATP titles looks to gain valuable points in his bid to qualify for the season-ending Nitto ATP Finals in Turin.

The 39-year-old Serbian, who captured the Basel title on his tournament debut in 2009, faces a tricky first-round encounter with French left-hander Ugo Humbert, a dangerous opponent known for his indoor hard-court prowess.

Djokovic, who has reached at least the final in all three of his Basel appearances, will be looking to make a deep run at the ATP 500 event, which begins Monday.

The Serbian icon is in tenth in the Race to Turin standings at the moment (when we account for Jannik Sinner’s absence) and is 319 points behind eighth place Rafael Jodar.

The Race to Turin will conclude after the Paris Masters, which will be played in eight days.

Meanwhile, Basel will also mark the final ATP appearance in Basel for three-time Grand Slam champion Stan Wawrinka.

The 41-year-old Swiss, affectionately known as the “Stanimal,” has reached two semifinals in Basel and owns a 17-17 career record at the tournament. He faces eighth seed Jiri Lehecka in a challenging first-round encounter.

The stakes are also high for several players chasing qualification for the Nitto ATP Finals in Turin.

Four contenders feature in the bottom half of the draw: sixth-place Arthur Fils, Jodar, 12th-place Taylor Fritz and 15th-place Alejandro Davidovich Fokina.

Fils, the second seed, opens against Hubert Hurkacz, while third seed Jodar faces Alejandro Tabilo in his opener. Fritz, seeded sixth and fresh off losing the Lyon final to Lorenzo Musetti, meets former World No. 3 Stefanos Tsitsipas in another marquee first-round clash.
