title: Unbeaten Edinburgh: 'There’s a long way to go... we will enjoy it while it lasts'
article_text:
Edinburgh Rugby remain top of the table after making it four wins out of four to equal their best start to a league season in 11 years.

They ran in five tries in beating the 10Bets Lions 31-10 at the Hive Stadium, with scrum-half Hector Patterson – who has just signed a contract extension – crossing twice in a Player of the Match performance.

Head coach Sean Everitt said: “It’s great that we are able to build momentum early in the competition. Momentum is always a good thing.

“There’s a long way to go, we know that.

“I am just happy that we got the result and, in these conditions, a bonus point too.

“The guys managed the game well and the passes stuck. I just thought they showed bravery with ball in hand.

“Then, in defence, to concede one try against a dangerous Lions team shows the effort the boys put in.”

Everitt added: “There’s a good vibe at the moment and obviously winning does bring that.

“We have been on the other side where we haven’t won every week or lost three or four in a row and that’s tough.

Glasgow Warriors have retained second spot after securing a dramatic late 24-20 victory over Benetton Rugby in Treviso.

They trailed 17-0 early in the second half and then 20-17 going into the dying embers of the game.

But, two minutes from time, replacement lock Jare Oguntibeju forced his way over to secure the victory and a four-try bonus point.

The Vodacom Bulls are in third after claiming the maximum haul in a 34-26 win against Ulster Rugby at Pretoria’s Loftus Versfeld.

It finished four tries apiece, with Bulls flanker Marcell Coetzee and Ulster winger Chay Mullins both crossing twice.

In the end, it was the place kicking of Springboks star Handre Pollard that proved the difference as he landed five successful shots at goal, while fellow fly-half Curwin Bosch added a last minute penalty to deny the visitors a second losing bonus point.

The DHL Stormers are in fourth after figuring in the highest scoring game of the weekend – a 52-40 victory over the Scarlets in Cape Town, where there were no fewer than 14 tries scored in all.

Having trailed 33-14 at the break, the Welsh visitors got it back to 40-40 with 14 minutes to go as centre Joe Roberts completed a hat-trick.

But a brace of late touchdowns from replacement fly-half Yaqeen Ahmed saw the Stormers come away with the spoils, leaving the six-try Scarlets having to settle for one losing bonus point.

The Hollywoodbets Sharks lie fifth having also come on strong in the latter stages, scoring three tries in the final quarter to secure a 36-21 bonus point victory over Cardiff Rugby at the Arms Park.

It was a notable scalp for the visitors from Durban as Cardiff hadn’t lost at home since last December.

Leinster’s win against Munster has taken them up to sixth, while the Ospreys have leapt into seventh spot with their own derby day triumph against Dragons RFC.

Completing the top eight are Connacht Rugby who ran in eight tries during a 48-27 win over Zebre Parma in Galway, with hooker Dave Heffernan snapping up a double.

In all, the eight URC games over the weekend produced a total of 456 points at an average of 57 points per game, while there were 69 tries scored at an average of 8.6 per match.

title: Alex Eala forced to withdraw from Pan Pacific Open event at the last minute
article_text:
Alex Eala and Desirae Krawcyzk will no longer participate in the women’s doubles event at the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo due to an injury.

The pair were due to team up for the first time and were set to face Hao-Ching Chan and Miyu Kato in their opening match on Monday morning, but they have been removed from the order of play as Krawcyzk has picked up an injury.

The American is struggling with a back problem with her decision coming barely 24 hours after she won the 14th WTA Tour doubles title of her career at the Ningbo Open.

The left-handed veteran teamed up with Fanny Stollar at the WTA 500 event in China with the pair beating top seeds Nicole Melichar-Martinez and Cristina Bucsa in the final on Sunday.

Eala, meanwhile, was looking to play her first doubles match since she partnered with Zeynep Sonmez at the Wuhan Open with the duo losing the opening round.

The Filipina will now instead focus on the singles tournament with her campaign kicking off on Monday afternoon when she takes on British wildcard Mika Stojsavljevic in the first round.

The world No 19 has struggled so far during the Asian swing as she has won only one match and that was last week in Ningbo when she beat Diane Parry in the first round before losing against sixth seed Diana Shnaider.

The 21-year-old lost her opening matches at the Singapore Open and Wuhan Open.

She is seeded eighth in Japan, and if she gets the better of the 17-year-old Stojsavljevic, then she will face Talia Gibson in the second round after the Australian defeated compatriot Daria Kasatkina in straight sets.

Eala has one tournament remaining after the Pan Pacific Open as she will head to Hong Kong next week for her second appearance at the WTA 250 event as she reached the second round on her debut 12 months ago.

Despite her struggles in Asia, the 2026 season has been another standout campaign for Eala as she won her first WTA Tour singles title at the Washington DC Open in August, beating Jessica Pegula in the final, while she also reached the fourth round at Wimbledon.

Eala was also a quarter-finalist at the Dubai Tennis Championships in February and made her top 20 debut in September after reaching the third round of the US Open.

title: Jannik Sinner confirmed to play exhibition match right before the Australian Open
article_text:
Jannik Sinner has been out of action for three months since lifting the Wimbledon title and fans will still have to wait a little while before seeing the Italian in action.

Sinner has already confirmed that he would end his 2026 season, although there have been some whispers about the star playing the delayed Six Kings Slam in Saudi Arabia at the end of December.

The Italian has appeared on marketing material for the exhibition event, which takes place in Riyad beween Sunday 27 December and Wednesday 30 December 2026.

Even if Sinner does not end up playing the Six Kings Slam, the star has been confirmed to play an exhibition match before the Australian Open kicks off.

The current world No 1 has already been slated for the One Point Slam and now he is set to play on the Rod Laver Arena during the Grand Slam’s ‘Opening Week’.

Sinner is set to play Felix Auger-Aliassime on Friday, January 15th, just two days before the main draw is set to begin.

With the Italian already confirming for the One Point Slam too, it’s clear that he is very confident that he will be back in time for the first Grand Slam of the 2027 season.

This is the second year in a row that Sinner will play Auger Aliassime in the Australian Open’s ‘Opening Week’.

The Italian won 6-4 4-6 10-4 in the exhibition match ahead of storming through to the semifinals of the Grand Slam, before he was beaten by Novak Djokovic.

It continued Sinner’s excellent record against Auger Aliassime, as he currently leads their head-to-head with five victories in their seven matches.

Sinner lost his first two matches to Auger Aliassime in 2022, at the Madrid Open and the Cincinnati Open, but he has won five straight matches against the Canadian star.

The Italian most recently knocked Auger Aliassime out of the quarterfinals of the Monte Carlo Masters en route to lifting the Masters title.

Sinner’s other victories against Auger Aliassime have come at the ATP Finals, the Paris Masters, the US Open, and the Cincinnati Open, so the Canadian’s hopes at majors and Masters have often been halted by the current world No 1.

In their last five matches together, Auger Aliassime has only managed to win one of the 12 sets he has played against Sinner, which is a worrying record.

Perhaps the Canadian will be using the Australian Open warm-up match as a way to work out how to finally play against one of the players he has struggled against the most on the ATP Tour.

title: wTVision looks to shape the future of sports broadcasting with Bronze SVG Europe sponsorship
article_text:
wTVision, a global provider of real-time broadcast graphics and media workflow solutions, has renewed its Bronze sponsorship of SVG Europe.

The company creates innovative solutions for the broadcast industry, focused on software development, graphics design and branding, live operations and human resources outsourcing. It takes part in more than 15,000 broadcasts annually and has experience in more than 120 countries.

Recent projects include introducing next-generation augmented reality graphics for the Jupiler Pro League in Belgium, and helping multiple broadcasters deliver more dynamic, informative and engaging coverage of the FIFA World Cup, contributing to live production, virtual studio environments, AR graphics, interactive analysis, channel operations and technical infrastructure.

“Sport is part of wTVision’s DNA. Our experience in live sports has shaped our belief that technology should give creativity more room to grow while keeping production teams in control. That vision guides our work, from real-time graphics and connected workflows to new possibilities in AI and immersive storytelling that bring fans closer to the action. Renewing our support for SVG Europe reflects our commitment to helping shape the future of sports broadcasting alongside the broadcasters, rights holders and technology partners who share that ambition,” Daniela Dias, marketing global manager at wTVision.
